children: said Wednesday it won’t pursue a public takeover offer for Arcadis
after failing to engage the Dutch engineering and consulting company in negotiations over a potential combination.

The Canadian engineering and infrastructure services company said it remains convinced that combining with Arcadis would have strategic benefits. However, WSP concluded that it couldn’t advance a transaction without support from Arcadis’ boards.

WSP had approached Arcadis about a potential deal but said it was unable to engage the company regarding transaction terms. WSP determined that pursuing an offer without negotiated support wouldn’t provide a viable path toward completing the combination.
The decision ends, at least for now, WSP’s effort to acquire Arcadis and create a larger global engineering, science and infrastructure services company.

WSP said it continues to see potential value in combining the two businesses, including benefits for shareholders, clients and employees. However, management emphasized that any transaction would need to be negotiated with Arcadis rather than pursued as an unsolicited public offer.

CEO Alexandre L'Heureux said WSP approached Arcadis because of what the company saw as the strategic and industrial merits of combining the businesses. He added that meaningful engagement from Arcadis was necessary before WSP could move forward.
WSP also reiterated that it intends to maintain a disciplined approach to acquisitions as it evaluates other opportunities.

For investors, the decision removes the near-term possibility that WSP will commit substantial capital to an Arcadis takeover or attempt to win shareholder support through a potentially prolonged unsolicited bid. It also leaves WSP free to pursue other acquisitions as part of its broader growth strategy.
Arcadis, meanwhile, remains independent after WSP concluded that a negotiated transaction wasn’t currently possible.

title: WSP drops pursuit of Arcadis after failing to secure deal talks
